instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Here We Go Again
cards.instruction: Use every new disagreement to prove the same relationship pattern is repeating, then raise the consequences.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've set the kitchen timer like you. Another twenty minutes keeping dinner warm. I'm always the one waiting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I set mine for the phone to charge. The battery died; that's why I didn't call.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, charging time. Last time it was the train. Tomorrow I'm eating at seven, whether you call or not.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll borrow a phone. Please keep a plate for me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll still be cooking and waiting. Miss another call and you can buy and cook your own dinner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've circled Sunday like you. Another confirmed visit for Mum to get ready for. Don't leave me explaining an empty bed again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I circled my new work shift. I can't visit on Sunday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, Sunday noted. Last time it was overtime. You call Mum and tell her this time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She'll think I don't want to come. Could you soften it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You cancel, I soften; here we go again. You can arrange the replacement visit with her too.

cards.title: Let Me Lean
cards.instruction: Get someone to carry part of the emotional burden without making you name how heavy it has become.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've crossed out today like you. That's our anniversary booking cancelled. Could you ring the restaurant as well?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I cross off days as they pass. You still need to cancel the table. What's happened?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, the phone part. Could that be the first thing you take off me? The number's on the fridge.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll call. Shall I ask for another date?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Say no for me. Then stay while I put the anniversary glasses away; you can tell me about your day.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've underlined the first line of this hospital letter like you did. Good news marked out. Read it before I do, would you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I underlined the reference number. Do you want me to read the letter aloud?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, start with the number. Then the words, as long as your face stays fairly ordinary.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll sit beside you. We can take one line at a time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep hold of the page too. I'll follow your finger; you don't need to ask why I'm so slow.

cards.title: Stay Until I’m Steady
cards.instruction: Keep someone present until you feel steady enough to face what comes next without them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my cup in the sink beside yours. Fresh cups for another round. Stay until I can tell the children about tomorrow's operation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm washing up because we're finished. We've had three rounds.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, finished with tea. Let me practise the first sentence on you before I fetch them.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My taxi's outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask for two minutes. Let me say 'I'll be in hospital' without stopping. Then I'll tell them myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I held my breath like you. Very calming, this new-flat routine. Stay while I try it again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was avoiding the paint smell. You need to breathe normally.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, fresh air first. Open the window with me before you go; I haven't been here on my own yet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll wait while you put the kettle on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stay until it boils. Then I'll try making one cup without getting yours out.

cards.title: Understand the Hurt
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge why their action hurt, not merely agree that it happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put a thumbs-up on your dinner message like you do. All dealt with. Do you understand why it hurt after I lost my job?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My thumbs-up means I've read it. I thought asking about dinner would give you something normal.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, received. But can you see why I heard a job for the cook instead of concern for me?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant we could go out. I'll book somewhere.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I believe you. Before you book, tell me you understand why I needed 'How are you?' first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've ticked your name like you ticked the others. That's the concert put behind us. Now tell me you understand why your empty seat hurt.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The ticks mean paid. I warned you that work might run late.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, paid seats. I still looked at yours before every song. You'd heard me practising for months.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You needed someone there who knew what it had taken.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You knew. Can you see why filling the seat with someone else wouldn't have helped?

cards.title: Tell Me I Did Enough
cards.instruction: Get someone to reassure you that your effort, choice, or survival was enough.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've ticked my painting on the list like yours. One complete contribution. Tell me that's enough for our exhibition.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The ticks mean insured. I can spread my paintings out so nobody sees a gap.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, safely covered. I want to know my painting contributes, not that you can hide how little I finished.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Put yours in the middle. It's the first one people should see.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then introduce me as the other painter. I'd like to hear it without an apology for only bringing one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You closed your copy of the speech, so I closed mine and finished. I stayed at the front. Was that enough?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I closed mine to put it on the chair. You skipped the last paragraph.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, copies away. I'm asking whether staying there counted; I nearly walked out before I started.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It counted. I'll help you practise that paragraph tomorrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could staying earn me tomorrow off? Tell me I can put the speech away for one day.
